# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1437 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1437 - **Title**: gh-1433 [GOAL] Workflow log fidelity: non-interactive headless renders EVERYTHING the model says — thinking deltas AND assistant text, default-on (the post-hoc log IS the UI) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1433` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 22 - **Additions**: +2207 - **Deletions**: -203 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T08:36:35Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-09T10:50:48Z ## PR Description Closes #1433 ### What changed A non-interactive `fa -p` log now reads back as the full narrative of what the agent did and said — thinking deltas (dimmed) and assistant text stream live with zero flags; nothing re-ordered, nothing swallowed, nothing only-at-the-end. Interactive faces keep their current byte shape. ### Key decisions - New pure seam `lib/src/cli/log_fidelity.dart`: `LogFidelityFace` (tui / interactiveLine / log) → `LogFidelity(streamThinking, liveText)`; `AgentCli` resolves it once and both render gates (`_streamsThinking`, `_buffersAnswer`) read from it — `resolveStreamThinking` now decides the interactive line-mode face only - AC3 positional fidelity: once a message streams a tool-call block, later text deltas hold until the tool RESULT renders (narration-after-tool lands after the result row); a non-`toolUse` message end flushes an orphaned hold (result-less turns swallow nothing); whitespace-only narration never paints a line (E1) - Escape hatches (E3 flag > env > face): `--no-stream-thinking` restores legacy thinking silence for one run (rejected together with `--stream-thinking`); `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy` reverts the whole headless face for edge log parsers; the reasoning-liveness line re-arms under the hatch (AC4) - Rendered deltas (thinking + held narration + live compaction summary, E4) pass through the SAME redaction pipeline as tool results, checked at render time (AC5/E6) - AC9/E7/E8: hub job cards grow a `CardTextFit` mode — the log face soft-wraps the FULL command and `log:` path (capped at 2000 chars with an explicit `(+N more chars, see )` pointer), the TUI pane keeps the width clip, and the card width seam now tracks the live `WindowSizeMsg` stream instead of the stale boot width - AC6: structured modes stay byte-identical — `HepEventsIO`/stream-json wrappers drop `write()` prose by contract (pinned by REG tests) ### How to verify ```bash dart test --exclude-tags integration # CI fast gate: 9763 passed, 0 failed dart test test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart # the AC/E matrix (29 tests) cd bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics # AC7 parser fixture: 20 tests ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RUN["fa -p / REPL / TUI"] --> FACE["resolveLogFidelityFace"] FACE --> LF["resolveLogFidelity
flag > env > face"] LF -->|log face| LIVE["thinking dimmed live + text live"] LF -->|interactiveLine| OPTIN["gh-1198 opt-in + buffered answer"] LF -->|tui| TUI["unchanged tiles"] LIVE --> HOLD["post-tool hold → result row → narration"] LIVE --> RED["redaction pipeline at render time"] ```
### Notes - Full-suite integration failures are NOT from this change — proven by `git worktree` bisect on clean `origin/main`: `headless_log_file` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e` (2), `headless_tools_flag` (2), `backend_mode_cli` (5) fail identically on main (ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` leak into the subprocess, a real provider answers instead of the mock); `browser_ext` (5) needs a Chrome service worker this runner cannot start; `subagent_integration` memory leg is the documented gh-1049 viewport-sampling flake (fails standalone on main too) - README + self-settings skill doc updated for the new default; `prompts.g.dart` regenerated (`prompts_sync_test` green)

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Two blocking issues: the `CRAP + duplication` CI gate is red (`ApprovalCommands._onMessageUpdate` grew to CC 16; the pinned 12.0 ratchet fails even at 100% coverage), and the new E8 width seam loses its `onResized` hook on the first model `copyWith` swap, so mid-run resizes are never tracked in production (the new UT drives the boot model, a path production never takes). Otherwise a well-tested change — the full AC/E matrix (AC1–AC7, AC9, E1–E4) is pinned by 29 green tests plus 20 bench parser tests, and AC6 stdout purity is backed by the real `HepEventsIO` host wiring.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 CI red: split `_onMessageUpdate` (CC 10 → 16) — unfixable by tests, CRAP ≥ CC at full coverage
- 🚨 E8: `FaTuiModel.copyWith` drops `onResized` → hook fires only for the startup resize
- ⚠️ Multi-tool-call narration flushes after the first result row (position drift)
- 💡 Card wrap budget starves the `log:` path; literal ESC byte in the Python fixture; redaction now touches interactive deltas (doc nuance)

**Next Steps**:
1. Split `_onMessageUpdate` into tool-gate / text / thinking helpers (repo precedent: `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd`)
2. Re-attach `onResized` in `copyWith` and pin the production swap path in the test
3. Non-blocking, for the follow-up card: the ticket's IT-TUI pty harness, IT-TUI-IMG image fixtures and the pty-less E2E were not delivered — the E8 swap-path bug is exactly the class of gap they would catch; the PR description's bench verify command should read `cd bench/terminal_bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics` (`cd bench` fails with ModuleNotFoundError)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `_onMessageUpdate` busts the CRAP ratchet — CI `CRAP + duplication` is red**

The guards job fails on this commit (`CRAP threshold exceeded: 16.00 > 12.0`, run 37906702478/job 113744954193). The offender is this method: cyclomatic complexity grew 10 → 16 with the AC3 hold logic, and CRAP ≥ CC even at 100% coverage (CI measured exactly `16.00 100.0`), so no test can ever green the pinned 12.0 ratchet ("only down from here", `crap4dart.yaml`).

Split the method along its three concerns, the same way `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` was split out of `_onAssistantMessageEnd` for the gh-1198 ratchet (the precedent is documented right below this method):

```dart
void _onMessageUpdate(AssistantMessageEvent e) {
  if (e is ToolCallStartEvent || e is ToolCallEndEvent) {
    _onToolCallGate(e);      // AC3 hold open/close (non-TUI)
    return;
  }
  if (e is TextDeltaEvent) { _onTextDelta(e); return; }        // live/hold/buffer paths
  if (e is ThinkingDeltaEvent && _streamsThinking) { _onThinkingDelta(e); }
}
```

Each helper lands well under CC 12 and behavior is unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the E8 live-width hook dies after the first model copy — mid-run resize is never tracked in production**

`FaTuiModel` is an immutable model: `update()` returns a `copyWith` copy and the program swaps to it (`_runningModel = nextModel` in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart:588`) — in fact `update()`'s busy-heartbeat alone re-copies the model on almost every message. `copyWith` does **not** carry `onResized` (it re-attaches `_wrapCache`, `_mouseRouter`, `_hitRegions`, … but not this new field), so:

1. Boot model (hook armed) processes the startup `scheduleResizeMsg()` → hook fires once.
2. The running model is now a copy with `onResized == null` → **every later SIGWINCH resize is silently dropped**; `_hubBlockWidth` freezes at the startup width.

E8's AC — "card after a window widen uses the new width, no restart needed" — is therefore not delivered, and the new UT cannot catch it because it drives `controller.model.update(...)` on the **boot instance**, a path production never takes (the returned copies are discarded in the test).

Fix: re-attach the hook in the `copyWith` tail alongside the other carried fields:

```dart
copy._mouseRouter = _mouseRouter;
copy.onResized = onResized; // gh-1433 E8: the seam must survive copies
```

and pin it by asserting the hook still fires on the model returned by `update(WindowSizeMsg(...))` (the production swap path).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: narration position drifts for messages with 2+ tool calls**

The hold is a single per-message buffer with no call attribution. For a message streaming `call1, call2, trailing text`, both calls' results render after message end, and the first `_onToolExecutionEnd` flushes the **entire** hold — narration that positionally belongs after result 2 lands between result 1 and result 2. The `(positional)` claim in the doc comment holds only for the single-call case AC3 tests.

Either track the pending call count and flush per result (the hold opens per `ToolCallStart`; deltas could record which call index they followed), or soften the comment to state the first-result approximation explicitly so a future reader does not trust it for parallel calls.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `log:` path is the first thing the 2000-char budget eats**

`_wrapCardBody` budgets the label first: a pathological multi-KB command (E7's own scenario) consumes the whole `logFaceCardMaxBodyChars`, so the `detail` — "the `log:` pointer is the thing a post-hoc reader follows" (AC9's words) — is exactly what gets `(+N more chars, see <log>)`-capped. Consider wrapping the detail first, or reserving it a slice of the budget, so the pointer survives even behind a huge command.

Minor: when `capped` flips mid-line, that physical line's trailing `\n` is never added to `overflow` (subsequent lines add `+1`), so the reported count can be off by one or two — cosmetic only.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the narration fixture embeds a literal ESC control byte**

`"I should check…"` here contains a raw `\x1b` character typed into the source (visible as `^[[2m` under `cat -v`), while the same file spells the identical escape explicitly 20 lines below (`"\x1b[2mthinking about the next step\x1b[0m"`). A literal control char is invisible in diffs and editors and is one accidental editor save away from corruption — use the `"\x1b[2m…\x1b[0m"` spelling for both fixture lines.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: redaction now also rides the interactive deltas — worth a doc line**

`_redactRendered` wraps both the text and the thinking delta for **every** face, and the pipeline is default-on (`buildRedactionPipeline` returns non-null unless `redact.enabled: false`). So the TUI/line-mode bytes change whenever a registered secret (e.g. the API key registered at boot) is echoed in a delta — a good security default, but it quietly contradicts "interactive faces keep their current byte shape" and the gh-1198 byte-pin for `--stream-thinking` sessions with redaction enabled. One sentence in the README flag docs / self-settings skill ("rendered deltas are redacted on all faces since gh-1433") keeps the byte-pin tests honest.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1437 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1437 - **Title**: gh-1433 [GOAL] Workflow log fidelity: non-interactive headless renders EVERYTHING the model says — thinking deltas AND assistant text, default-on (the post-hoc log IS the UI) - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1433` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 22 - **Additions**: +2207 - **Deletions**: -203 - **Created**: 2026-10-09T08:36:35Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-09T10:50:48Z ## PR Description Closes #1433 ### What changed A non-interactive `fa -p` log now reads back as the full narrative of what the agent did and said — thinking deltas (dimmed) and assistant text stream live with zero flags; nothing re-ordered, nothing swallowed, nothing only-at-the-end. Interactive faces keep their current byte shape. ### Key decisions - New pure seam `lib/src/cli/log_fidelity.dart`: `LogFidelityFace` (tui / interactiveLine / log) → `LogFidelity(streamThinking, liveText)`; `AgentCli` resolves it once and both render gates (`_streamsThinking`, `_buffersAnswer`) read from it — `resolveStreamThinking` now decides the interactive line-mode face only - AC3 positional fidelity: once a message streams a tool-call block, later text deltas hold until the tool RESULT renders (narration-after-tool lands after the result row); a non-`toolUse` message end flushes an orphaned hold (result-less turns swallow nothing); whitespace-only narration never paints a line (E1) - Escape hatches (E3 flag > env > face): `--no-stream-thinking` restores legacy thinking silence for one run (rejected together with `--stream-thinking`); `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy` reverts the whole headless face for edge log parsers; the reasoning-liveness line re-arms under the hatch (AC4) - Rendered deltas (thinking + held narration + live compaction summary, E4) pass through the SAME redaction pipeline as tool results, checked at render time (AC5/E6) - AC9/E7/E8: hub job cards grow a `CardTextFit` mode — the log face soft-wraps the FULL command and `log:` path (capped at 2000 chars with an explicit `(+N more chars, see )` pointer), the TUI pane keeps the width clip, and the card width seam now tracks the live `WindowSizeMsg` stream instead of the stale boot width - AC6: structured modes stay byte-identical — `HepEventsIO`/stream-json wrappers drop `write()` prose by contract (pinned by REG tests) ### How to verify ```bash dart test --exclude-tags integration # CI fast gate: 9763 passed, 0 failed dart test test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart # the AC/E matrix (29 tests) cd bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics # AC7 parser fixture: 20 tests ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RUN["fa -p / REPL / TUI"] --> FACE["resolveLogFidelityFace"] FACE --> LF["resolveLogFidelity
flag > env > face"] LF -->|log face| LIVE["thinking dimmed live + text live"] LF -->|interactiveLine| OPTIN["gh-1198 opt-in + buffered answer"] LF -->|tui| TUI["unchanged tiles"] LIVE --> HOLD["post-tool hold → result row → narration"] LIVE --> RED["redaction pipeline at render time"] ```
### Notes - Full-suite integration failures are NOT from this change — proven by `git worktree` bisect on clean `origin/main`: `headless_log_file` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e` (2), `headless_tools_flag` (2), `backend_mode_cli` (5) fail identically on main (ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` leak into the subprocess, a real provider answers instead of the mock); `browser_ext` (5) needs a Chrome service worker this runner cannot start; `subagent_integration` memory leg is the documented gh-1049 viewport-sampling flake (fails standalone on main too) - README + self-settings skill doc updated for the new default; `prompts.g.dart` regenerated (`prompts_sync_test` green)

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1437._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 9 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Two blocking issues: the `CRAP + duplication` CI gate is red (`ApprovalCommands._onMessageUpdate` grew to CC 16; the pinned 12.0 ratchet fails even at 100% coverage), and the new E8 width seam loses its `onResized` hook on the first model `copyWith` swap, so mid-run resizes are never tracked in production (the new UT drives the boot model, a path production never takes). Otherwise a well-tested change — the full AC/E matrix (AC1–AC7, AC9, E1–E4) is pinned by 29 green tests plus 20 bench parser tests, and AC6 stdout purity is backed by the real `HepEventsIO` host wiring.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 CI red: split `_onMessageUpdate` (CC 10 → 16) — unfixable by tests, CRAP ≥ CC at full coverage
- 🚨 E8: `FaTuiModel.copyWith` drops `onResized` → hook fires only for the startup resize
- ⚠️ Multi-tool-call narration flushes after the first result row (position drift)
- 💡 Card wrap budget starves the `log:` path; literal ESC byte in the Python fixture; redaction now touches interactive deltas (doc nuance)

**Next Steps**:
1. Split `_onMessageUpdate` into tool-gate / text / thinking helpers (repo precedent: `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd`)
2. Re-attach `onResized` in `copyWith` and pin the production swap path in the test
3. Non-blocking, for the follow-up card: the ticket's IT-TUI pty harness, IT-TUI-IMG image fixtures and the pty-less E2E were not delivered — the E8 swap-path bug is exactly the class of gap they would catch; the PR description's bench verify command should read `cd bench/terminal_bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics` (`cd bench` fails with ModuleNotFoundError)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `_onMessageUpdate` busts the CRAP ratchet — CI `CRAP + duplication` is red**

The guards job fails on this commit (`CRAP threshold exceeded: 16.00 > 12.0`, run 37906702478/job 113744954193). The offender is this method: cyclomatic complexity grew 10 → 16 with the AC3 hold logic, and CRAP ≥ CC even at 100% coverage (CI measured exactly `16.00 100.0`), so no test can ever green the pinned 12.0 ratchet ("only down from here", `crap4dart.yaml`).

Split the method along its three concerns, the same way `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` was split out of `_onAssistantMessageEnd` for the gh-1198 ratchet (the precedent is documented right below this method):

```dart
void _onMessageUpdate(AssistantMessageEvent e) {
  if (e is ToolCallStartEvent || e is ToolCallEndEvent) {
    _onToolCallGate(e);      // AC3 hold open/close (non-TUI)
    return;
  }
  if (e is TextDeltaEvent) { _onTextDelta(e); return; }        // live/hold/buffer paths
  if (e is ThinkingDeltaEvent && _streamsThinking) { _onThinkingDelta(e); }
}
```

Each helper lands well under CC 12 and behavior is unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the E8 live-width hook dies after the first model copy — mid-run resize is never tracked in production**

`FaTuiModel` is an immutable model: `update()` returns a `copyWith` copy and the program swaps to it (`_runningModel = nextModel` in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart:588`) — in fact `update()`'s busy-heartbeat alone re-copies the model on almost every message. `copyWith` does **not** carry `onResized` (it re-attaches `_wrapCache`, `_mouseRouter`, `_hitRegions`, … but not this new field), so:

1. Boot model (hook armed) processes the startup `scheduleResizeMsg()` → hook fires once.
2. The running model is now a copy with `onResized == null` → **every later SIGWINCH resize is silently dropped**; `_hubBlockWidth` freezes at the startup width.

E8's AC — "card after a window widen uses the new width, no restart needed" — is therefore not delivered, and the new UT cannot catch it because it drives `controller.model.update(...)` on the **boot instance**, a path production never takes (the returned copies are discarded in the test).

Fix: re-attach the hook in the `copyWith` tail alongside the other carried fields:

```dart
copy._mouseRouter = _mouseRouter;
copy.onResized = onResized; // gh-1433 E8: the seam must survive copies
```

and pin it by asserting the hook still fires on the model returned by `update(WindowSizeMsg(...))` (the production swap path).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: narration position drifts for messages with 2+ tool calls**

The hold is a single per-message buffer with no call attribution. For a message streaming `call1, call2, trailing text`, both calls' results render after message end, and the first `_onToolExecutionEnd` flushes the **entire** hold — narration that positionally belongs after result 2 lands between result 1 and result 2. The `(positional)` claim in the doc comment holds only for the single-call case AC3 tests.

Either track the pending call count and flush per result (the hold opens per `ToolCallStart`; deltas could record which call index they followed), or soften the comment to state the first-result approximation explicitly so a future reader does not trust it for parallel calls.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `log:` path is the first thing the 2000-char budget eats**

`_wrapCardBody` budgets the label first: a pathological multi-KB command (E7's own scenario) consumes the whole `logFaceCardMaxBodyChars`, so the `detail` — "the `log:` pointer is the thing a post-hoc reader follows" (AC9's words) — is exactly what gets `(+N more chars, see <log>)`-capped. Consider wrapping the detail first, or reserving it a slice of the budget, so the pointer survives even behind a huge command.

Minor: when `capped` flips mid-line, that physical line's trailing `\n` is never added to `overflow` (subsequent lines add `+1`), so the reported count can be off by one or two — cosmetic only.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the narration fixture embeds a literal ESC control byte**

`"I should check…"` here contains a raw `\x1b` character typed into the source (visible as `^[[2m` under `cat -v`), while the same file spells the identical escape explicitly 20 lines below (`"\x1b[2mthinking about the next step\x1b[0m"`). A literal control char is invisible in diffs and editors and is one accidental editor save away from corruption — use the `"\x1b[2m…\x1b[0m"` spelling for both fixture lines.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: redaction now also rides the interactive deltas — worth a doc line**

`_redactRendered` wraps both the text and the thinking delta for **every** face, and the pipeline is default-on (`buildRedactionPipeline` returns non-null unless `redact.enabled: false`). So the TUI/line-mode bytes change whenever a registered secret (e.g. the API key registered at boot) is echoed in a delta — a good security default, but it quietly contradicts "interactive faces keep their current byte shape" and the gh-1198 byte-pin for `--stream-thinking` sessions with redaction enabled. One sentence in the README flag docs / self-settings skill ("rendered deltas are redacted on all faces since gh-1433") keeps the byte-pin tests honest.

---

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.

<   }

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {

<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();

<     }
<   }

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Key Issues**:

- 🚨 E8: `FaTuiModel.copyWith` drops `onResized` → hook fires only for the startup resize

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `_onMessageUpdate` busts the CRAP ratchet — CI `CRAP + duplication` is red**

The guards job fails on this commit (`CRAP threshold exceeded: 16.00 > 12.0`, run 37906702478/job 113744954193). The offender is this method: cyclomatic complexity grew 10 → 16 with the AC3 hold logic, and CRAP ≥ CC even at 100% coverage (CI measured exactly `16.00 100.0`), so no test can ever green the pinned 12.0 ratchet ("only down from here", `crap4dart.yaml`).

Split the method along its three concerns, the same way `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` was split out of `_onAssistantMessageEnd` for the gh-1198 ratchet (the precedent is documented right below this method):

```dart
void _onMessageUpdate(AssistantMessageEvent e) {
  if (e is ToolCallStartEvent || e is ToolCallEndEvent) {
    _onToolCallGate(e);      // AC3 hold open/close (non-TUI)
    return;
  }
  if (e is TextDeltaEvent) { _onTextDelta(e); return; }        // live/hold/buffer paths
  if (e is ThinkingDeltaEvent && _streamsThinking) { _onThinkingDelta(e); }
}
```

Each helper lands well under CC 12 and behavior is unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the E8 live-width hook dies after the first model copy — mid-run resize is never tracked in production**

`FaTuiModel` is an immutable model: `update()` returns a `copyWith` copy and the program swaps to it (`_runningModel = nextModel` in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart:588`) — in fact `update()`'s busy-heartbeat alone re-copies the model on almost every message. `copyWith` does **not** carry `onResized` (it re-attaches `_wrapCache`, `_mouseRouter`, `_hitRegions`, … but not this new field), so:

1. Boot model (hook armed) processes the startup `scheduleResizeMsg()` → hook fires once.
2. The running model is now a copy with `onResized == null` → **every later SIGWINCH resize is silently dropped**; `_hubBlockWidth` freezes at the startup width.

E8's AC — "card after a window widen uses the new width, no restart needed" — is therefore not delivered, and the new UT cannot catch it because it drives `controller.model.update(...)` on the **boot instance**, a path production never takes (the returned copies are discarded in the test).

Fix: re-attach the hook in the `copyWith` tail alongside the other carried fields:

```dart
copy._mouseRouter = _mouseRouter;
copy.onResized = onResized; // gh-1433 E8: the seam must survive copies
```

and pin it by asserting the hook still fires on the model returned by `update(WindowSizeMsg(...))` (the production swap path).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: narration position drifts for messages with 2+ tool calls**

The hold is a single per-message buffer with no call attribution. For a message streaming `call1, call2, trailing text`, both calls' results render after message end, and the first `_onToolExecutionEnd` flushes the **entire** hold — narration that positionally belongs after result 2 lands between result 1 and result 2. The `(positional)` claim in the doc comment holds only for the single-call case AC3 tests.

Either track the pending call count and flush per result (the hold opens per `ToolCallStart`; deltas could record which call index they followed), or soften the comment to state the first-result approximation explicitly so a future reader does not trust it for parallel calls.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `log:` path is the first thing the 2000-char budget eats**

`_wrapCardBody` budgets the label first: a pathological multi-KB command (E7's own scenario) consumes the whole `logFaceCardMaxBodyChars`, so the `detail` — "the `log:` pointer is the thing a post-hoc reader follows" (AC9's words) — is exactly what gets `(+N more chars, see <log>)`-capped. Consider wrapping the detail first, or reserving it a slice of the budget, so the pointer survives even behind a huge command.

Minor: when `capped` flips mid-line, that physical line's trailing `\n` is never added to `overflow` (subsequent lines add `+1`), so the reported count can be off by one or two — cosmetic only.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the narration fixture embeds a literal ESC control byte**

`"I should check…"` here contains a raw `\x1b` character typed into the source (visible as `^[[2m` under `cat -v`), while the same file spells the identical escape explicitly 20 lines below (`"\x1b[2mthinking about the next step\x1b[0m"`). A literal control char is invisible in diffs and editors and is one accidental editor save away from corruption — use the `"\x1b[2m…\x1b[0m"` spelling for both fixture lines.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: redaction now also rides the interactive deltas — worth a doc line**

`_redactRendered` wraps both the text and the thinking delta for **every** face, and the pipeline is default-on (`buildRedactionPipeline` returns non-null unless `redact.enabled: false`). So the TUI/line-mode bytes change whenever a registered secret (e.g. the API key registered at boot) is echoed in a delta — a good security default, but it quietly contradicts "interactive faces keep their current byte shape" and the gh-1198 byte-pin for `--stream-thinking` sessions with redaction enabled. # pr-1437: gh-1433 [GOAL] Workflow log fidelity: non-interactive headless renders EVERYTHING the model says — thinking deltas AND assistant text, default-on (the post-hoc log IS the UI) ## Description Closes #1433 ### What changed A non-interactive `fa -p` log now reads back as the full narrative of what the agent did and said — thinking deltas (dimmed) and assistant text stream live with zero flags; nothing re-ordered, nothing swallowed, nothing only-at-the-end. Interactive faces keep their current byte shape. ### Key decisions - New pure seam `lib/src/cli/log_fidelity.dart`: `LogFidelityFace` (tui / interactiveLine / log) → `LogFidelity(streamThinking, liveText)`; `AgentCli` resolves it once and both render gates (`_streamsThinking`, `_buffersAnswer`) read from it — `resolveStreamThinking` now decides the interactive line-mode face only - AC3 positional fidelity: once a message streams a tool-call block, later text deltas hold until the tool RESULT renders (narration-after-tool lands after the result row); a non-`toolUse` message end flushes an orphaned hold (result-less turns swallow nothing); whitespace-only narration never paints a line (E1) - Escape hatches (E3 flag > env > face): `--no-stream-thinking` restores legacy thinking silence for one run (rejected together with `--stream-thinking`); `FA_LOG_FIDELITY=legacy` reverts the whole headless face for edge log parsers; the reasoning-liveness line re-arms under the hatch (AC4) - Rendered deltas (thinking + held narration + live compaction summary, E4) pass through the SAME redaction pipeline as tool results, checked at render time (AC5/E6) - AC9/E7/E8: hub job cards grow a `CardTextFit` mode — the log face soft-wraps the FULL command and `log:` path (capped at 2000 chars with an explicit `(+N more chars, see )` pointer), the TUI pane keeps the width clip, and the card width seam now tracks the live `WindowSizeMsg` stream instead of the stale boot width - AC6: structured modes stay byte-identical — `HepEventsIO`/stream-json wrappers drop `write()` prose by contract (pinned by REG tests) ### How to verify ```bash dart test --exclude-tags integration # CI fast gate: 9763 passed, 0 failed dart test test/cli/workflow_log_fidelity_test.dart # the AC/E matrix (29 tests) cd bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics # AC7 parser fixture: 20 tests ```
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD RUN["fa -p / REPL / TUI"] --> FACE["resolveLogFidelityFace"] FACE --> LF["resolveLogFidelity
flag > env > face"] LF -->|log face| LIVE["thinking dimmed live + text live"] LF -->|interactiveLine| OPTIN["gh-1198 opt-in + buffered answer"] LF -->|tui| TUI["unchanged tiles"] LIVE --> HOLD["post-tool hold → result row → narration"] LIVE --> RED["redaction pipeline at render time"] ```
### Notes - Full-suite integration failures are NOT from this change — proven by `git worktree` bisect on clean `origin/main`: `headless_log_file` (4), `yolo_rm_critical_e2e` (2), `headless_tools_flag` (2), `backend_mode_cli` (5) fail identically on main (ambient `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`/`FA_LOG_FILE` leak into the subprocess, a real provider answers instead of the mock); `browser_ext` (5) needs a Chrome service worker this runner cannot start; `subagent_integration` memory leg is the documented gh-1049 viewport-sampling flake (fails standalone on main too) - README + self-settings skill doc updated for the new default; `prompts.g.dart` regenerated (`prompts_sync_test` green)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||

<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():

<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1437._

> ℹ️ **6 resolved thread(s) excluded; 9 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 7

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Two blocking issues: the `CRAP + duplication` CI gate is red (`ApprovalCommands._onMessageUpdate` grew to CC 16; the pinned 12.0 ratchet fails even at 100% coverage), and the new E8 width seam loses its `onResized` hook on the first model `copyWith` swap, so mid-run resizes are never tracked in production (the new UT drives the boot model, a path production never takes). Otherwise a well-tested change — the full AC/E matrix (AC1–AC7, AC9, E1–E4) is pinned by 29 green tests plus 20 bench parser tests, and AC6 stdout purity is backed by the real `HepEventsIO` host wiring.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 CI red: split `_onMessageUpdate` (CC 10 → 16) — unfixable by tests, CRAP ≥ CC at full coverage
- 🚨 E8: `FaTuiModel.copyWith` drops `onResized` → hook fires only for the startup resize
- ⚠️ Multi-tool-call narration flushes after the first result row (position drift)
- 💡 Card wrap budget starves the `log:` path; literal ESC byte in the Python fixture; redaction now touches interactive deltas (doc nuance)

**Next Steps**:
1. Split `_onMessageUpdate` into tool-gate / text / thinking helpers (repo precedent: `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd`)
2. Re-attach `onResized` in `copyWith` and pin the production swap path in the test
3. Non-blocking, for the follow-up card: the ticket's IT-TUI pty harness, IT-TUI-IMG image fixtures and the pty-less E2E were not delivered — the E8 swap-path bug is exactly the class of gap they would catch; the PR description's bench verify command should read `cd bench/terminal_bench && python3 -m unittest test_bench_metrics` (`cd bench` fails with ModuleNotFoundError)

---


## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `_onMessageUpdate` busts the CRAP ratchet — CI `CRAP + duplication` is red**

The guards job fails on this commit (`CRAP threshold exceeded: 16.00 > 12.0`, run 37906702478/job 113744954193). The offender is this method: cyclomatic complexity grew 10 → 16 with the AC3 hold logic, and CRAP ≥ CC even at 100% coverage (CI measured exactly `16.00 100.0`), so no test can ever green the pinned 12.0 ratchet ("only down from here", `crap4dart.yaml`).

Split the method along its three concerns, the same way `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` was split out of `_onAssistantMessageEnd` for the gh-1198 ratchet (the precedent is documented right below this method):

```dart
void _onMessageUpdate(AssistantMessageEvent e) {
  if (e is ToolCallStartEvent || e is ToolCallEndEvent) {
    _onToolCallGate(e);      // AC3 hold open/close (non-TUI)
    return;
  }
  if (e is TextDeltaEvent) { _onTextDelta(e); return; }        // live/hold/buffer paths
  if (e is ThinkingDeltaEvent && _streamsThinking) { _onThinkingDelta(e); }
}
```

Each helper lands well under CC 12 and behavior is unchanged.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

🚨 **BLOCKING: the E8 live-width hook dies after the first model copy — mid-run resize is never tracked in production**

`FaTuiModel` is an immutable model: `update()` returns a `copyWith` copy and the program swaps to it (`_runningModel = nextModel` in `vendor/dart_tui/lib/src/program.dart:588`) — in fact `update()`'s busy-heartbeat alone re-copies the model on almost every message. `copyWith` does **not** carry `onResized` (it re-attaches `_wrapCache`, `_mouseRouter`, `_hitRegions`, … but not this new field), so:

1. Boot model (hook armed) processes the startup `scheduleResizeMsg()` → hook fires once.
2. The running model is now a copy with `onResized == null` → **every later SIGWINCH resize is silently dropped**; `_hubBlockWidth` freezes at the startup width.

E8's AC — "card after a window widen uses the new width, no restart needed" — is therefore not delivered, and the new UT cannot catch it because it drives `controller.model.update(...)` on the **boot instance**, a path production never takes (the returned copies are discarded in the test).

Fix: re-attach the hook in the `copyWith` tail alongside the other carried fields:

```dart
copy._mouseRouter = _mouseRouter;
copy.onResized = onResized; // gh-1433 E8: the seam must survive copies
```

and pin it by asserting the hook still fires on the model returned by `update(WindowSizeMsg(...))` (the production swap path).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: narration position drifts for messages with 2+ tool calls**

The hold is a single per-message buffer with no call attribution. For a message streaming `call1, call2, trailing text`, both calls' results render after message end, and the first `_onToolExecutionEnd` flushes the **entire** hold — narration that positionally belongs after result 2 lands between result 1 and result 2. The `(positional)` claim in the doc comment holds only for the single-call case AC3 tests.

Either track the pending call count and flush per result (the hold opens per `ToolCallStart`; deltas could record which call index they followed), or soften the comment to state the first-result approximation explicitly so a future reader does not trust it for parallel calls.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the `log:` path is the first thing the 2000-char budget eats**

`_wrapCardBody` budgets the label first: a pathological multi-KB command (E7's own scenario) consumes the whole `logFaceCardMaxBodyChars`, so the `detail` — "the `log:` pointer is the thing a post-hoc reader follows" (AC9's words) — is exactly what gets `(+N more chars, see <log>)`-capped. Consider wrapping the detail first, or reserving it a slice of the budget, so the pointer survives even behind a huge command.

Minor: when `capped` flips mid-line, that physical line's trailing `\n` is never added to `overflow` (subsequent lines add `+1`), so the reported count can be off by one or two — cosmetic only.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: the narration fixture embeds a literal ESC control byte**

`"I should check…"` here contains a raw `\x1b` character typed into the source (visible as `^[[2m` under `cat -v`), while the same file spells the identical escape explicitly 20 lines below (`"\x1b[2mthinking about the next step\x1b[0m"`). A literal control char is invisible in diffs and editors and is one accidental editor save away from corruption — use the `"\x1b[2m…\x1b[0m"` spelling for both fixture lines.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-09):

💡 **SUGGESTION: redaction now also rides the interactive deltas — worth a doc line**

`_redactRendered` wraps both the text and the thinking delta for **every** face, and the pipeline is default-on (`buildRedactionPipeline` returns non-null unless `redact.enabled: false`). So the TUI/line-mode bytes change whenever a registered secret (e.g. the API key registered at boot) is echoed in a delta — a good security default, but it quietly contradicts "interactive faces keep their current byte shape" and the gh-1198 byte-pin for `--stream-thinking` sessions with redaction enabled. One sentence in the README flag docs / self-settings skill ("rendered deltas are redacted on all faces since gh-1433") keeps the byte-pin tests honest.

---

Fixed on this head — the method is split along the three concerns, following
the `_flushAssistantStreamAtEnd` precedent:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
