blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.
<   void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     reasoning.progress();
<     streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
<   }
< 
<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {
<           streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<         } else {
<           streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

<   /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider

<   /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over

<   void compactionLivenessStart() {

<     // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.
<   void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     reasoning.progress();
<     streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
<   }

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {

<         } else {

<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

blocks.text:
# Office add-in (Outlook taskpane) acceptance suite (issues #89, #182):
# the taskpane IS the fa Flutter web app (outlook/app/) — validates the
# manifest, builds the app bundle with the office host flag, runs the
# office package Dart unit tests, the app's office wiring tests, and
# Playwright (chromium + webkit) against the assembled pane pages.
# Path-filtered so unrelated pushes skip it.
name: Office add-in

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'office_addin/**'
      - 'flutter_app/**'
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'lib/**'
      - 'pubspec.lock'
      - 'scripts/build_office_addin.sh'
      - '.github/workflows/office-addin.yml'
  workflow_dispatch:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same ref (issue #177) — but a
# workflow_dispatch run (the daily-publish addin leg) gets its OWN group:
# a push landing mid-daily used to cancel the leg's run, failing the leg
# as "higher priority waiting request exists" and self-filing a false
# release issue (issue #423).
concurrency:
  group: Office add-in-${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && format('dispatch-{0}', github.run_id) || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal permissions (artifact uploads only).
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  office-addin-suite:
    name: Office add-in suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily addin watcher's budget arithmetic (#351):
    # dart + chrome-platform tests + add-in build + Playwright
    # chromium/webkit install & e2e; historically ~20m.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: stable
          cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # office_addin/dart is a separate package (path dep on this root),
      # so its pub get must follow the root's.
      - name: dart pub get (root)
        run: dart pub get

      - name: Dart unit tests (office_addin/dart)
        run: cd office_addin/dart && dart pub get && dart test

      # The app build needs the gitignored placeholders (.env asset and
      # firebase_options.dart) — same dance pages.yml does.
      - name: App placeholders (.env + firebase_options)
        run: |
          touch [REDACTED:Credential File]
          cp flutter_app/firebase_options.template.dart flutter_app/lib/firebase_options.dart

      # gh-1310 rework (review thread 2): resolve flutter_app through the
      # shared retry action BEFORE the first flutter consumer — the package
      # config doesn't exist at checkout, so "Chrome boot tests" would
      # otherwise trigger flutter test's implicit (unenforced, unretried)
      # pub get first.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # The office boot seam compiles web-only code, so its guard tests run
      # on the chrome platform (VM suite can't import them). FA_HOST=office
      # compiles the real boot branch in; Office.js is absent in the test
      # browser, pinning the clean office_unavailable failure path.
      - name: Chrome boot tests (flutter_app/test/web)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/web --platform chrome --dart-define=FA_HOST=office

      - name: Office wiring tests (flutter_app)
        run: cd flutter_app && flutter test test/services/office_wiring_test.dart

      # Validates the manifest (fails loudly on any issue), builds the
      # fa web app with FA_HOST=office and assembles the site slice —
      # the artifact under test AND the upload below.
      - name: Build Office add-in
        run: bash scripts/build_office_addin.sh

      # chromium + webkit: Outlook on the web runs the taskpane in
      # whichever engine the browser has, so both must boot the pane.
      - name: Playwright e2e (chromium + webkit)
        run: |
          cd office_addin/e2e
          npm ci
          npx playwright install --with-deps chromium webkit
          npx playwright test --reporter=line

      - name: Upload assembled add-in
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: office-addin
          path: build/pages/root/outlook/

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.

<   }

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {

<         } else {

<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.
<   void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     reasoning.progress();
<     streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
<   }
< 
<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {
<           streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<         } else {
<           streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

<   /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
<   /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
<   /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
<   /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent

<   void compactionLivenessStart() {

<     // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
<     // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
<     // --stream-thinking runs.

+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||

+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }

+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The

+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();

<   /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.
<   void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     reasoning.progress();
<     streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
<   }
< 
<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {
<           streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<         } else {
<           streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

<   /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]

+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }

+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
<   /// stop it.
<   void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     reasoning.progress();
<     streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
<   }
< 
<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {
<           streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<         } else {
<           streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<         }
<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }
< 
<   /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
<   /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
<   /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
<   /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
<   /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
<   /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
<   /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
<   /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
<   void compactionLivenessStart() {
<     // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
<     // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
<     // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
<     // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
<     // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
<     // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
<     // --stream-thinking runs.

<   /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot

<   /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
<   /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
<   /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
<   /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
<   void compactionLivenessEnd() {
<     reasoning.stop();
<   }

+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):

<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():

{"patch":"[lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart#49A5]
INS.POST 161:
+
+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }

+  /// Test seam: fires one stream-liveness evaluation now (gh-1430), the
+  /// analog of [reasoningLivenessTickForTest].

+  /// Test seam: whether the stream heartbeat is armed right now (gh-1430)
+  /// — the request-out/rendered-output observable.
+  @visibleForTesting
+  bool get streamLivenessActiveForTest => _waiting.streamHeartbeat.armed;
+
+  /// Test seam: whether an unrendered event arrived in the heartbeat's
+  /// window since the last print (gh-1430) — the aliveness observable an
+  /// integration test waits on after pushing a stream event.
+  @visibleForTesting

+    final heart = _waiting.streamHeartbeat;
+    // ignore: invalid_use_of_visible_for_testing_member

<   /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
<   /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
<   /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
<   /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends

<   }

<   /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
<   /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
<   /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
<   /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
<   /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
<   /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
<   /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
<   /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
<   /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
<   void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
<     switch (event) {
<       case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
<         final rendered =
<             assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
<             (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
<                 _cli._streamsThinking);
<         if (rendered) {

<       case MessageStartEvent():
<         // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
<         streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
<       case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
<         streamHeartbeat.stop();
<       case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
<         // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
<         streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
<       default:
<         break;
<     }
<   }

{"patch":"[lib/src/cli/agent_cli_waiting.dart#49A5]
INS.POST 161:
+
+  /// Streaming-phase liveness (gh-1430): the fifth waiting horizon — a
+  /// provider request whose events flow but render NOTHING in the current
+  /// output mode (thinking deltas with `--stream-thinking` off, the
+  /// headless default). Tier 2 disarms at the first event, which is
+  /// exactly when a reasoning burst starts, so the pane used to go
+  /// byte-silent for minutes of healthy streaming. The heartbeat prints
+  /// `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` on the same waiting cadence — and never
+  /// for a stream that stopped emitting, so fa's stream-idle watchdog
+  /// stays the sole arbiter of stream death.
+  late final StreamLivenessHeartbeat streamHeartbeat = StreamLivenessHeartbeat(
+    onRemind: (elapsed) => _printLiveness(streamLivenessLine(elapsed)),
+    clock: _clock,
+    livenessSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessSeconds,
+    tickSeconds: () => _cli.config.waiting.toolLivenessTickSeconds,
+  );
SWAP 163.=177:
+  /// A provider request went out (gh-1198 + gh-1430): arm both watches
+  /// when this surface watches them — surfaces where thinking does NOT
+  /// render. Since gh-1433 that is decided by the SAME log-fidelity
+  /// resolution the render gate uses: TUI and log-face runs (headless)
+  /// see the deltas (or tiles) live; only non-streaming line mode and
+  /// the `--no-stream-thinking` hatch watch the silent window.
+  void reasoningRequestStarted() {
+    if (_cli._streamsThinking) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+    streamHeartbeat.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// Any agent event after the request (gh-1198): tier 2 watches only the
+  /// pre-first-event window, so ANY event is visible progress for it. The
+  /// stream heartbeat classifies instead (gh-1430): rendered output
+  /// disarms it, unrendered stream events prove aliveness, lifecycle ends
+  /// stop it.
+  void reasoningProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    reasoning.progress();
+    streamHeartbeatProgress(event);
+  }
+
+  /// The gh-1430 classification of one agent event for the stream
+  /// heartbeat. Rendered (disarm): text deltas (raw mode prints them
+  /// live; styled surfaces flush at message end — either way the answer
+  /// is on its way, E1), streamed thinking deltas, and tool rows. Live
+  /// but unrendered: the stream events headless does not draw. Stops:
+  /// the message/turn ends — the request phase is over, and a timer that
+  /// prints over an ended stream would be a wall timer, not a liveness
+  /// signal. Everything else (run bookkeeping, tool heartbeats) is
+  /// neither, and leaves the watch untouched.
+  void streamHeartbeatProgress(AgentEvent event) {
+    switch (event) {
+      case MessageUpdateEvent(:final assistantMessageEvent):
+        final rendered =
+            assistantMessageEvent is TextDeltaEvent ||
+            (assistantMessageEvent is ThinkingDeltaEvent &&
+                _cli._streamsThinking);
+        if (rendered) {
+          streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+        } else {
+          streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+        }
+      case MessageStartEvent():
+        // Mirrors the provider stream's StartEvent: the first byte landed.
+        streamHeartbeat.unrenderedEvent();
+      case MessageEndEvent() || TurnEndEvent() || AgentEndEvent():
+        streamHeartbeat.stop();
+      case ToolExecutionStartEvent() || ToolExecutionEndEvent():
+        // The tool rows print in every mode — rendered bytes.
+        streamHeartbeat.renderedOutput();
+      default:
+        break;
+    }
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window (gh-1430 E3): summarizer requests are provider
+  /// requests too, but NO agent events fire while the [AutoCompactor]
+  /// runs — neither tracker would ever see its stream. Arm tier 2 over
+  /// the window so a multi-minute summarization is not a byte-silent
+  /// bench window: past the cadence it prints the bare `… reasoning Ns`
+  /// line until the window ends (a dead summarizer stream errors through
+  /// fa's own watchdog first, same as the main path). Line mode/headless
+  /// only — the TUI busy row (`Compacting context…`) owns that surface.
+  void compactionLivenessStart() {
+    // Deliberately ignores config.streamThinking (unlike
+    // reasoningRequestStarted): the summarizer's stream never reaches
+    // the CLI render path, so nothing renders in this window even with
+    // the flag on — tier 2 is the only signal here. Do NOT add the
+    // streamThinking gate for "consistency": it would silently
+    // reintroduce a byte-silent multi-minute summarization window in
+    // --stream-thinking runs.
+    if (_cli._useTui) return;
+    reasoning.requestStarted();
+  }
+
+  /// The compaction window ended: drop the watch (a stale arm cannot
+  /// survive into the idle session — the next agent event disarms tier 2
+  /// anyway, but the explicit stop keeps the chain honest). The
+  /// unconditional stop (no `streamThinking`/TUI guard) is safe by
+  /// lifecycle: compaction runs BETWEEN provider requests — the watch is
+  /// disarmed outside the window anyway, so the stop is a belt-and-
+  /// braces no-op unless a compaction ever overlaps an in-flight request.
+  void compactionLivenessEnd() {
+    reasoning.stop();
+  }
